intro: A malfunctioning garage door opener causes immediate disruption. Whether your garage serves as a main entry point for a suburban home or secures an alley parking spot in the city, a broken opener is a problem. We fix openers for residential garages throughout Chicago and the surrounding suburbs. Our technicians diagnose the issue, explain the necessary repair, and provide a flat-rate quote before any work begins. We work on all major opener brands and models. Issues can range from a simple remote failure to a worn drive system to electrical component failure. A properly working opener offers daily convenience and security. When it fails, daily routines are interrupted. Our service restores your opener's full function and safety quickly. We carry common replacement parts on our trucks to complete most repairs on the first visit. We are available Monday through Saturday, 24 hours a day, for urgent service needs.
whatWeDo: We repair garage door openers when components fail. Drive gears wear out, especially in older chain drive units. These often fail due to age and repeated stress, causing the motor to hum without moving the door. Safety sensor pairs can become misaligned or damaged, leading to the door reversing or not closing at all. Logic boards can fail due to power surges or age, affecting remote responsiveness or overall operation. Belts and chains stretch or break, preventing the trolley from engaging the door. Trolley carriages can crack or seize, stopping the door's movement along the rail. Our service addresses these specific failures. A full repair includes replacing the failed part with a new, compatible component. The typical repair price, including parts, ranges from $120 to $320. This price varies based on the specific part needed and the complexity of the replacement. For example, replacing a logic board might be at the higher end, while sensor replacement is often at the lower end. We only install new, quality parts.

problemSigns.sign: Opener hums, door does not move
problemSigns.detail: This often indicates a stripped drive gear or a motor issue preventing power transfer to the drive system.

problemSigns.sign: Door reverses before touching the floor
problemSigns.detail: Safety sensors may be misaligned, obstructed, or have a wiring problem. The opener detects an issue and reverses.
This can be a dead battery, a programming error, or a logic board failure within the opener unit itself.
Blinking lights usually signal a fault with the safety sensors. This prevents the door from closing properly for safety reasons.
The trolley carriage is likely disconnected or broken. This prevents the opener from physically engaging and lifting the garage door.

faqs.q: What determines the cost of opener repair?
faqs.a: The repair cost depends on the specific part that needs replacement. More complex components like logic boards or full drive gear assemblies are typically more expensive than safety sensors. Our flat-rate quote covers parts and labor.

faqs.q: How long does an opener repair take?
faqs.a: Most opener repairs are completed within 1-2 hours. Our trucks carry common parts, which allows for efficient service on the first visit.

faqs.q: Can I repair my garage door opener myself?
faqs.a: Opener repairs involve electrical components and heavy moving parts. Incorrect repairs can cause further damage or pose safety risks. Professional repair ensures correct parts and proper function.

faqs.q: How long do garage door openers typically last?
faqs.a: Most garage door openers last 10-15 years. Regular use, maintenance, and environmental factors can affect lifespan. Older units may begin to have more frequent component failures.

faqs.q: Is it better to repair or replace an old opener?
faqs.a: If an opener is nearing the end of its typical lifespan (10-15 years) or requires multiple expensive repairs, replacement might be more cost-effective. We can advise you on the best option after diagnosis.
